source.name: ArrowDown moves one calendar week across the end of daylight saving time
source.scope: Post-hoc task added after an independent review (2026-10-24) found that, in Europe/London, ArrowDown from Friday 23 October 2026 selected Thursday 29 October: Pikaday adds 24-hour millisecond blocks, so the end of British Summer Time on 25 October shifts the result one day back. The defect exists in the pinned upstream component and was preserved by the earlier model patches. Source is the original consumer with the final model-authored component from run 459ef2eb attempt 3. Withheld UTC, London and closed-range checks were frozen before inference and omitted from the model request. Not blind or production-customer evidence.

journey.title: ArrowDown moves one calendar week across the end of daylight saving time
journey.goal: Weekends are closed. Arrow keys move by calendar days (ArrowLeft/Right one day, ArrowUp/Down one week) in the user time zone, including across daylight-saving changes, then skip closed days in the same direction. Preserve pointer selection and the other field.

functionalJourney.title: Available weekday selection preserves actual booking dates
functionalJourney.goal: Weekends are closed. Arrow keys move by calendar days (ArrowLeft/Right one day, ArrowUp/Down one week) in the user time zone, including across daylight-saving changes, then skip closed days in the same direction. Preserve pointer selection and the other field.

plan.root_cause: The adjustDate function in pikaday.js adds days by adding milliseconds (UTC), which does not account for daylight saving time transitions. When crossing a DST boundary, adding 7 days worth of milliseconds can result in a local date that is off by one day, causing ArrowDown to land on 2026-10-29 instead of the expected 2026-10-30.
plan.repair_strategy: Replace the adjustDate to adjustDate to perform calendar-day arithmetic by manipulating the date's year, month, and day fields. This ensures that adding 7 days moves the local date by exactly 7 calendar days regardless of DST changes. The while loop that skips disabled days (weekends) is also updated to use calendar-day increments.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard navigation for date pickers will correctly move by weeks across DST boundaries, ensuring users can select dates predictably and consistently with WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Changing date arithmetic may affect other uses of adjustDate (e.g., single-day arrows). However, the new method is more correct for all cases.
Risk of off-by-one in other scenarios is low because the Date constructor handles month/year rollover.
verification_requirements: Test ArrowDown on a date before DST end (e.g., 2026-10-22) results in 2026-10-30 (not 2026-10-29).
Test single-day arrows (ArrowLeft/Right) across DST boundaries.
Verify that weekend skipping still works correctly.
